title: SAMe Synthesis
pm_id: BRS2-FM1-PM3
mission: 'Maintain methionine adenosyltransferase capacity to convert methionine and ATP into SAMe, sustaining the methyl-donor pool used by downstream methyltransferases.'
parent_fm: BRS2(FM1)
parent_brs: BRS2
evidence_status: stage-2b-dietary-addressability
summary: 'Methionine adenosyltransferase forms S-adenosylmethionine from methionine and ATP. Magnesium and potassium ions coordinate that ATP-dependent catalysis. This reaction supplies the methyl donor used by many later enzymes. Upstream methionine regeneration and later methyl-transfer reactions remain separate processes. Circulating SAMe and the SAM:SAH ratio describe pool balance rather than synthesis speed.'

scientific_findings_intro: 'Human MAT structural and kinetic studies identify reaction participants, while kinetic models disagree about substrate-binding order. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) [[2]](#pm-ref-2) These studies directly establish enzyme mechanism and biochemical requirements. They do not test ordinary dietary modulation, human in-vivo synthesis flux or downstream methylation outcomes, so those effects remain beyond the evidence summarised here.'
scientific_findings:
  - id: PM3-F1
    finding_label: 'Biochemical provenance: MAT reaction'
    presentation: mechanistic-basis
    fm_rollup: true
    finding_summary: MAT-dependent SAMe synthesis directly requires methionine and ATP and uses active-site magnesium and potassium ions to support ATP-dependent catalysis.
    finding_interpretation: 'This establishes the biochemical reaction and its direct requirements. It does not establish that increasing dietary methionine, magnesium or potassium increases SAMe synthesis in adequately nourished humans; ATP is an intracellular biochemical substrate, not a dietary lever.'

  - id: PM3-IC1
    finding_label: 'SAM and SAM:SAH are pool-state markers, not synthesis-flux measures'
    presentation: interpretive-constraint
    finding_statement: 'Measured SAM concentration and the SAM:SAH ratio reflect the balance of synthesis, methyl-group utilisation, SAH formation and clearance and therefore cannot by themselves identify MAT-dependent SAMe synthesis capacity.'
    synthesised_evidence_confidence: not-yet-scored
    synthesis: 'SAM concentration is a metabolite-pool measurement. The SAM:SAH ratio is commonly interpreted as a methylation index because SAM supplies methyl groups while SAH inhibits methyltransferases. Both values integrate production and consumption processes; neither is a direct MAT flux assay. Careful sample handling is also material because SAM is unstable under neutral and alkaline conditions.'
    synthesis_limitations: 'The principal source is a methods and profiling study, not a formal validation against isotope-traced MAT flux. The ratio may be useful for methyl-group homeostasis and inherited-metabolism assessment, but its exact meaning varies by biological matrix, compartment and pre-analytical handling.'

          study: LC-MS/MS method optimisation plus a randomised four-week vegan-versus-meat-rich dietary intervention.
          population: Method reference cohort of 33 healthy adults and dietary intervention cohort of 53 healthy adult omnivores aged 18–60 years.

  - id: PM3-F4

    finding_summary: Folate and betaine remethylation regenerate methionine upstream of MAT-dependent SAMe formation; choline can contribute through betaine.

    synthesis: 'Existing reviewed PM1-F1, PM2-F1/PM2-F2 and PM3-F1 establish the successive reaction identities. ## BRS2-1-3 - SAMe Synthesis

(Producing the Cell's Methyl-Donor Pool)

## 1. Mission & Overview

### Mission

Maintain methionine adenosyltransferase capacity to convert methionine and ATP into SAMe, sustaining the methyl-donor pool used by downstream methyltransferases.


**Intervention Dominance:** Diet-Supported

### Overview

Methionine adenosyltransferase forms S-adenosylmethionine from methionine and ATP. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) Magnesium and potassium ions coordinate that ATP-dependent catalysis. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) [[2]](#pm-ref-2) This reaction supplies the methyl donor used by many later enzymes. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) Upstream methionine regeneration and later methyl-transfer reactions remain separate processes. Circulating SAMe and the SAM:SAH ratio describe pool balance rather than synthesis speed. [[3]](#pm-ref-3)

- **Benefits:** Forming SAMe provides the common methyl donor used by many different enzymes. [[4]](#pm-ref-4) Those later uses include DNA methylation, membrane-phospholipid formation, and neurotransmitter metabolism.
- **Implementation Notes:** Methionine and dietary protein are the provision routes. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) Magnesium and potassium ions take part in the catalysis and are not separate dosing targets. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) [[2]](#pm-ref-2) These reaction requirements do not set an intake for raising SAMe synthesis. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) [[3]](#pm-ref-3)

## 4. Mechanistic Basis + Scientific Findings

### Summary

SAMe production is the point at which methionine and intracellular ATP become a usable methyl donor. The defining event is MAT catalysis; upstream regeneration of methionine and downstream consumption of SAMe determine context but are not part of the synthesis reaction itself.

<div class="brs-fm-hub-item" data-brs-fm-hub>
<div class="brs-fm-hub-shell">
<button type="button" class="brs-fm-hub-summary" aria-expanded="false">
<span class="brs-fm-hub-chevron" aria-hidden="true"></span>
<strong>SAMe synthesis — mechanistic detail</strong>
</button>
<div class="brs-fm-hub-panel" hidden>

<span id="pm3-mechanism-f1" />
<span id="methionine-adenosyltransferase-reaction" />

#### PM3-F1

MAT catalyses an ATP-dependent reaction in which methionine's sulfur attacks ATP's adenosyl carbon to form SAMe; phosphate products are subsequently released. Human MAT2A studies support conflicting ATP-first and rapid-equilibrium random substrate-binding models; no settled universal order is asserted. See [PM3-F1](#pm3-f1). Human MATα2 structures capture catalytic states and active-site ion coordination [[2](#pm-ref-2)].


Supporting evidence: [PM3-F1](#pm3-f1).

#### (Direct requirements and capacity)

Methionine and ATP are reaction substrates. Magnesium and potassium ions participate in active-site phosphate coordination under biochemical and structural conditions [[1](#pm-ref-1), [2](#pm-ref-2)]. These are biochemical requirements, not evidence that ordinary dietary magnesium, potassium or methionine intake is rate-limiting. MAT isoform abundance, enzyme stability, substrate availability and feedback all contribute to cellular capacity; the reviewed evidence does not establish a simple human basal-versus-reserve dietary threshold.

<span id="pm3-mechanism-f5" />

#### PM3-F5

MAT2B association can preserve MAT2A protein or catalytic stability in purified-human-enzyme and mammalian-cell experiments. This supports a stability contribution to enzyme regulation, not an exclusive explanation of MAT2B action or a demonstrated increase in human SAMe synthesis flux. Bailey et al. (2021) [[1]](#pm-ref-1); 10.1038/s41419-024-07093-8 [[11]](#pm-ref-11); 10.1107/S2052252526005075 [[12]](#pm-ref-12); 10.1021/acs.biochem.0c00998 [[13]](#pm-ref-13)

Supporting evidence: [PM3-F5](#pm3-f5).

#### (Pool state is not synthesis flux)

SAM concentration reflects formation and consumption. The SAM:SAH ratio additionally incorporates SAH production and clearance and is commonly used as a methylation-potential index, not a direct measure of MAT flux. Accurate interpretation also depends on matrix and sample handling because SAM is unstable [[3](#pm-ref-3)].

#### (Boundaries of the mechanism)

This PM governs methionine → SAMe formation through MAT. Folate/B12-dependent remethylation belongs to [BRS2-FM1-PM1](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm1-folate-b12-dependent-homocysteine-remethylation); betaine/BHMT remethylation to [BRS2-FM1-PM2](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation); integrated methionine-cycle throughput to [BRS2-FM1-PM4](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm4-methionine-cycle-flux); and transsulfuration to [BRS2-FM2-PM5](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm2/brs2-fm2-pm5-transsulfuration-pathway). PEMT, DNA, neurotransmitter and other methyl-transfer reactions are downstream consumers, not SAMe synthesis.

<span id="pm3-mechanism-f4" />
<span id="integration-within-brs2" />

#### PM3-F4

Within [BRS2(FM1) — Methylation Cycle Efficiency](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-methylation-cycle-efficiency), PM1 and PM2 regenerate methionine, PM3 converts it to SAMe, and PM4 represents integrated cycle flux. [BRS2(KC2) — Methionine & Transsulfuration Substrate Pool](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/kc/brs2-kc2-methionine-transsulfuration-substrate-pool) supplies substrate context without proving dietary control of PM3.


Supporting evidence: [PM3-F4](#pm3-f4).

### 4.1 Scientific Findings

#### Summary

Human MAT structural and kinetic studies identify reaction participants, while kinetic models disagree about substrate-binding order. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) [[2]](#pm-ref-2) These studies directly establish enzyme mechanism and biochemical requirements. They do not test ordinary dietary modulation, human in-vivo synthesis flux or downstream methylation outcomes, so those effects remain beyond the evidence summarised here.

### 5.1 BRS Pathways

[BRS2-FM1-PM1 — Folate/B12-Dependent Homocysteine Remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm1-folate-b12-dependent-homocysteine-remethylation) / [BRS2-FM1-PM2 — Betaine/BHMT Remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation)<br />
↓<br />
**BRS2-FM1-PM3 — SAMe Synthesis**<br />
↓<br />
[BRS2-FM1-PM4 — Methionine Cycle Flux](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm4-methionine-cycle-flux)

### 5.2 Cross-BRS Mechanism Relationships

- [BRS-X(Circadian-FM1-PM3) — Melatonin Biosynthesis & Availability](/docs/biological-targets/brs-x/circadian/fm1/brs-x-circadian-fm1-pm3-melatonin-biosynthesis-and-availability) — ASMT uses SAM as a methyl donor. That is an upstream biochemical dependency. Folate, B12, B6 and iron are not admitted on Circadian PM3.

### 5.3 Local BRS Mechanism Relationships

- [BRS2-FM1-PM1 — Folate/B12-Dependent Homocysteine Remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm1-folate-b12-dependent-homocysteine-remethylation) — Remethylates homocysteine to methionine that can enter SAM synthesis. Upstream methionine supply, not the MAT step itself.
- [BRS2-FM1-PM2 — Betaine/BHMT Remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation) — Alternative remethylation route to methionine. Parallel supply, not SAM synthetase activity.
- [BRS2-FM1-PM4 — Methionine Cycle Flux](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm4-methionine-cycle-flux) — Consumes and regenerates methionine around SAM-using reactions. Shared one-carbon resource, not this PM’s synthesis reaction.

## 7. Phenome Connections

These mappings are translational relationships, not single-mechanism outcome claims. Phenomes are emergent functional patterns supported by multiple interacting PMs across the BRAIN Framework.

    relationship_type: modulates
    confidence: low-medium

    evidence_confidence: low-medium
    rationale: 'SAM donates methyl groups, and homocysteine is then split between remethylation and transsulfuration {{cite:chiang_s-adenosylmethionine_1996,finkelstein_homocysteine_1998}}. Homocysteine concentration is discussed as a risk marker for cognitive decline and Alzheimer disease {{cite:luzzi_homocysteine_2022,yu_evidence-based_2020}}. Those studies measure a metabolite level. They do not measure branch rates, and they do not show that changing cycle throughput improves Cognitive Clarity.'

    established_links:

      - 'Folic acid lowered blood homocysteine concentration, with a further concentration reduction when vitamin B12 was added (PM4-IC1).'
      - Stam 2005 directly measured higher whole-body remethylation and transmethylation after folic acid; the earlier concentration-only account is incomplete.

    disposition: unresolved
    established_links:
      - Methionine is the amino acid from which SAM and then homocysteine are formed (PM4-F1).
      - A liver MAT isoenzyme allows excess methionine to continue SAM synthesis (PM4-F1).
      - 'In aged mice, too little or too much methionine removed benefits of a low-amino-acid longevity diet on frailty and metabolic signalling (connected evidence on PM4-F1).'
      - Lamers 2011 measured human methionine-cycle rates and shows context-dependent preservation under moderate B6 restriction; it did not manipulate the sulfur pool.
    inferred_links:

scientific_findings:
  - id: PM4-F1
    finding_label: Homocysteine is split between remethylation and transsulfuration
    presentation: mechanistic-basis
    fm_rollup: true
    finding_summary: 'Methionine becomes SAM, SAM donates a methyl group, and SAH is hydrolysed to homocysteine. Homocysteine is then either remethylated to methionine or sent into transsulfuration toward cysteine.'
    finding_interpretation: 'This is the integrated route and the branch. It does not assign the MAT, remethylation or transsulfuration reactions to this mechanism, and it does not show that ordinary diet changes the rates.'
    finding_statement: 'Methionine-cycle throughput runs from methionine to SAM, methyl transfer and SAH hydrolysis to homocysteine, after which homocysteine is distributed between remethylation and transsulfuration under the influence of SAM, SAH and methyl-tetrahydrofolate.'
    synthesised_evidence_confidence: not-yet-scored
    synthesis: 'A methylation review establishes SAM as the methyl donor and SAH hydrolysis to adenosine and homocysteine, and it shows that blocking that hydrolysis can affect methylation of phospholipids, proteins, DNA, RNA and small molecules together. A pathway review then places regulation at the distribution of homocysteine between remethylation, which every tissue can perform, and transsulfuration to cystathionine, which is limited to liver, kidney, small intestine and pancreas, with SAM, SAH and methyl-tetrahydrofolate as effectors. A human tracer study uses that same partition, measuring postprandial remethylation, transmethylation and total transsulfuration as rates.'
    synthesis_limitations: 'The pathway accounts are reviews. Transsulfuration is not present in every tissue. The human rate study was a 28-day vitamin B6 restriction in nine healthy young adults. It does not show that ordinary changes in methionine, folate, or B-vitamin intake change those rates. Individual enzyme reactions remain neighbouring mechanisms.'
    evidence_considered:
      - label: Chiang et al. (1996)
        citation_key: chiang_s-adenosylmethionine_1996
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#chiang_s-adenosylmethionine_1996
        data_level: Mechanistic
        evidence_source: repository-inherited
        directional_finding: 'SAM donates methyl groups; SAH formed by that transfer is hydrolysed to adenosine and homocysteine; blocking SAH hydrolysis can affect methylation across phospholipids, proteins, DNA, RNA and small molecules.'
        assessment:
          study: 'Narrative review of SAM-dependent methylation, SAH hydrolysis and downstream methyl acceptors.'
          population: Review of biochemical and cellular literature; no new human cohort.
          result: SAM is the methyl donor. SAH is hydrolysed by SAH hydrolase to adenosine and homocysteine. Blocking that hydrolase can affect methylation of several classes of acceptor at once.
          effect_magnitude: No quantitative flux or concentration effect size.
          evidence_summary: Establishes methyl transfer and the SAH-to-homocysteine step as a shared route into many methylation reactions.
          limitations: 'Does not describe remethylation, transsulfuration or a measured SAM:SAH ratio, and does not test diet or cognition.'
      - label: Finkelstein (1998)
        citation_key: finkelstein_homocysteine_1998
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#finkelstein_homocysteine_1998
        data_level: Mechanistic
        evidence_source: bounded-external-search
        directional_finding: 'Homocysteine is distributed between tissue-wide remethylation and transsulfuration to cystathionine in liver, kidney, small intestine and pancreas; SAM, SAH and methyl-tetrahydrofolate are effectors of that distribution.'
        assessment:
          study: Review of mammalian methionine-cycle and transsulfuration pathways and their regulation.
          population: Mammalian pathway review; no new human experiment.
          result: 'Every tissue can synthesise SAM, use it for transmethylation, hydrolyse SAH and remethylate homocysteine. Transsulfuration catabolises homocysteine in liver, kidney, small intestine and pancreas. Regulation is the distribution of homocysteine between remethylation and conversion to cystathionine.'
          effect_magnitude: No numeric rate or intake-response estimate.
          evidence_summary: 'Establishes the regulated branch between recycling and transsulfuration and names SAM, SAH and methyl-tetrahydrofolate as effectors.'
          limitations: 'Review-level pathway evidence. It does not measure human rates, test ordinary diets, or show a cognitive or attention outcome.'

        citation_key: lamers_vitamin_b6_methionine_cycle_2011

## 1. Mission & Overview + Dietary Levers

### Overview

The methionine cycle forms S-adenosylmethionine from methionine, transfers its methyl group, and hydrolyses S-adenosylhomocysteine to adenosine and homocysteine. [[2]](#pm-ref-2) Homocysteine is then remethylated to methionine or sent into transsulfuration toward cysteine. [[12]](#pm-ref-12) SAM, SAH and methyl-tetrahydrofolate influence that split. [[12]](#pm-ref-12) Every tissue can remethylate homocysteine, while transsulfuration is limited to liver, kidney, small intestine and pancreas. [[12]](#pm-ref-12) Metabolite concentrations describe pool state, not the branch rates. [[13]](#pm-ref-13)

- **Benefits:** Maintaining methionine-cycle flux lets cells keep donating methyl groups while directing sulfur toward cysteine. [[2]](#pm-ref-2) [[12]](#pm-ref-12) That coordination helps keep methylation and sulfur exit together.
- **Implementation Notes:** Methionine, dietary protein, vitamin B9 (folate), vitamin B12 (cobalamin), vitamin B6, and vitamin B2 (riboflavin) are the provision routes. [[6]](#pm-ref-6) [[13]](#pm-ref-13) Folic acid and vitamin B12 can lower blood homocysteine, and moderate vitamin B6 restriction can raise cystathionine, without a shown change in those branch rates. [[6]](#pm-ref-6) [[13]](#pm-ref-13)
- **Biological Relevance:** [SAMe formation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm3-same-synthesis), each remethylation reaction, and the [transsulfuration enzyme steps](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm2/brs2-fm2-pm5-transsulfuration-pathway) are neighbouring mechanisms. [[12]](#pm-ref-12)

## 2. Primary Biological Effects

↑ coordinated throughput from methionine through SAM to homocysteine<br />
↔ distribution of homocysteine between remethylation and transsulfuration<br />
→ methylation continues while SAH is hydrolysed onward

## 4. Mechanistic Basis

### Summary

Methyl-group use and sulfur exit meet at homocysteine. What matters is how that intermediate is divided between return to methionine and transsulfuration, with SAM, SAH and methyl-tetrahydrofolate as effectors of the split.

<div class="brs-fm-hub-item" data-brs-fm-hub>
<div class="brs-fm-hub-shell">
<button type="button" class="brs-fm-hub-summary" aria-expanded="false">
<span class="brs-fm-hub-chevron" aria-hidden="true"></span>
<strong>Methionine cycle flux — mechanistic detail</strong>
</button>
<div class="brs-fm-hub-panel" hidden>

#### (From methionine to homocysteine)

Methionine is converted to S-adenosylmethionine (SAM), the principal methyl donor. After the methyl group is transferred, S-adenosylhomocysteine (SAH) is hydrolysed to adenosine and homocysteine. Blocking that hydrolysis can affect methylation of phospholipids, proteins, DNA, RNA and small molecules together [Chiang et al. (1996) [[2]](#pm-ref-2)].

#### (The regulated split)

Every tissue can remethylate homocysteine back to methionine. Transsulfuration, which converts homocysteine to cystathionine and onward toward cysteine, occurs in liver, kidney, small intestine and pancreas. Regulation is the distribution of homocysteine between those exits. SAM, SAH and methyl-tetrahydrofolate are effectors of that distribution [Finkelstein (1998) [[12]](#pm-ref-12)]. Human postprandial studies can measure the same partition as remethylation, transmethylation and total transsulfuration rates [Lamers et al. (2011) [[13]](#pm-ref-13)].

#### (Concentrations and rates)

Folic acid lowers blood homocysteine concentration, and vitamin B12 adds a further concentration reduction, while added vitamin B6 does not [Collaboration (1998) [[6]](#pm-ref-6)]. A small trial also reported lower plasma homocysteine after vitamin B12, fish oil, or both [Huang et al. (2015) [[11]](#pm-ref-11)]. In the tracer study, cystathionine concentration rose during vitamin B6 restriction while the mean total transsulfuration rate did not [[13]](#pm-ref-13). A concentration change is a different result from a branch rate.

#### (Boundaries of the mechanism)

This mechanism is the integrated throughput and the split at homocysteine. Formation of SAM is [BRS2-FM1-PM3 — SAMe Synthesis](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm3-same-synthesis). Folate- and vitamin B12-dependent remethylation is [BRS2-FM1-PM1 — Folate/B12-Dependent Homocysteine Remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm1-folate-b12-dependent-homocysteine-remethylation). Betaine-dependent remethylation is [BRS2-FM1-PM2 — Betaine/BHMT Remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation). The transsulfuration reactions are [BRS2-FM2-PM5 — Transsulfuration Pathway](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm2/brs2-fm2-pm5-transsulfuration-pathway). Methionine-restriction experiments in ageing models, and homocysteine associations with dementia or ADHD, do not show that changing these rates treats a cognitive or attention disorder [Fanti et al. (2026) [[3]](#pm-ref-3); Luzzi et al. (2022) [[8]](#pm-ref-8); Lukovac et al. (2024) [[9]](#pm-ref-9)].

#### (Integration within methylation cycle efficiency)

SAM synthesis feeds this throughput. Remethylation returns homocysteine to methionine, and transsulfuration is the catabolic exit. Downstream methyl acceptors include phospholipids, proteins, DNA and RNA [Chiang et al. (1996) [[2]](#pm-ref-2)]. The parent account of methylation cycle efficiency is [BRS2(FM1) — Methylation Cycle Efficiency](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-methylation-cycle-efficiency).

</div>
</div>

### 4.1 Scientific Findings

#### Summary

A controlled human tracer study found unchanged mean postprandial remethylation, transmethylation and transsulfuration rates during moderate vitamin B6 restriction, despite sharply reduced plasma PLP and increased cystathionine concentration. [[13]](#pm-ref-13) Pathway reviews provide the regulatory context for these measured branch rates. [[2]](#pm-ref-2) [[12]](#pm-ref-12) The combined evidence shows why an altered intermediate concentration cannot be treated as an equivalent change in overall cycle flux; individual responses and the restriction conditions limit generalisation.

### 5.1 BRS Pathways

[BRS2-FM1-PM3 — SAMe Synthesis](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm3-same-synthesis)<br />
↓<br />

↓<br />
[BRS2-FM1-PM1 — Folate/B12-Dependent Homocysteine Remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm1-folate-b12-dependent-homocysteine-remethylation) / [BRS2-FM1-PM2 — Betaine/BHMT Remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation)<br />
↓<br />
or [BRS2-FM2-PM5 — Transsulfuration Pathway](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm2/brs2-fm2-pm5-transsulfuration-pathway)

### 5.2 Cross-BRS Mechanism Relationships

Primary Mechanisms in other Biological Regulatory Systems that directly interact with, constrain or support this mechanism.

- None listed

### 5.3 Local BRS Mechanism Relationships

Related Primary Mechanisms within the same Biological Regulatory System that collectively support the integrated biological function.

- [BRS2-FM1-PM1 — Folate/B12-Dependent Homocysteine Remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm1-folate-b12-dependent-homocysteine-remethylation) — Remethylates homocysteine to methionine and thereby carries one recycling exit. The split between that exit and transsulfuration is the upstream allocation.
- [BRS2-FM1-PM2 — Betaine/BHMT Remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation) — Remethylates homocysteine to methionine by a betaine-dependent route that runs parallel to folate-dependent recycling and stays separate from transsulfuration.
- [BRS2-FM1-PM3 — SAMe Synthesis](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm3-same-synthesis) — Produces SAM from methionine and ATP. That SAM is the methyl donor consumed as throughput moves from methyl transfer to homocysteine and the branch.
- [BRS2-FM2-PM5 — Transsulfuration Pathway](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm2/brs2-fm2-pm5-transsulfuration-pathway) — Carries homocysteine onward to cystathionine and cysteine after the branch has directed it into transsulfuration, which is the catabolic exit rather than the recycling arm.

## 7. Phenome Connections

These mappings are translational relationships, not single-mechanism outcome claims. Phenomes are emergent functional patterns supported by multiple interacting PMs across the BRAIN Framework.

---
title: Gut Barrier / Tight Junction Integrity
pm_id: BRS5-FM1-PM1
mission: Maintain epithelial tight junction integrity and selective permeability at the gut lining.
summary: >-
  The gut lining is a selective gate. Tight junctions, the seals between its cells, control which materials
  pass between them. Maintaining that selectivity helps protect the body while allowing normal exchange.
  Butyrate, cellular zinc and retinoid signalling affect epithelial functions in experimental models;
  glutamine has a condition-specific human permeability result. These findings identify different biological
  routes rather than a universal gut-repair supplement.
parent_fm: BRS5(FM1)
parent_brs: BRS5
key_constraints:
  - BRS5(KC1)
cofactors: []

      oral/dietary lever. The microbial, active-metabolite or selected supplementation context is preserved;
      applicability requires resolution.
    dietary_input_flags:
      - section-supply-contradiction
    input: Butyrate
    input_type: substrate
    biological_role: >-
      Microbially produced short-chain fatty acid that serves as a colonocyte energy substrate and directly
      promotes intestinal tight-junction assembly.
    evidence_source:
      finding_ids:
        - PM1-F2
      citation_keys:
        - peng_butyrate_2009
        - silva_role_2020
    evidence_limitation: >-
      Direct evidence includes a Caco-2 monolayer model and broader mechanistic synthesis; it does not
      establish that oral butyrate is required, that ordinary intake predictably changes epithelial exposure,
      or a human intake threshold for PM1.
    canonical_identity:
      status: resolved

scientific_findings_intro: >-
  Butyrate and zinc experiments directly interrogate epithelial junction function. Retinoids influence
  differentiation and permeability, but their direction depends on the model. A selected postinfectious IBS
  trial found a glutamine response; heterogeneous supplementation evidence does not support a general regimen.
  Microbiota associations do not establish a barrier-to-cognition effect. [[4]](#pm-ref-4) [[1]](#pm-ref-1)
  [[5]](#pm-ref-5) [[2]](#pm-ref-2) [[6]](#pm-ref-6) Alcohol studies identify a context-specific barrier
  stressor and recovery relationship; carotenoid absorption supports upstream delivery, and fermented-milk
  findings remain preparation- and population-specific.
scientific_findings:
  - id: PM1-F1
    finding_label: Tight junctions govern selective paracellular permeability
    presentation: mechanistic-basis
    fm_rollup: false
    finding_summary: >-
      Intestinal epithelial tight junctions form regulated pore and leak pathways that determine selective
      paracellular passage.
    finding_interpretation: >-
      This supports the PM boundary around epithelial gate function. Downstream microbial-product containment
      and systemic inflammation remain outside it.
    finding_statement: >-
      Intestinal tight-junction structure and regulation determine selective paracellular permeability, while
      epithelial injury can create a distinct unrestricted permeability pathway.
    synthesised_evidence_confidence: not-yet-scored
    synthesis: >-
      An authoritative mechanistic review distinguishes tight-junction-dependent pore and leak pathways from
      unrestricted flux caused by epithelial damage. In a mouse pneumonia model, increased permeability and
      claudin-2 were attenuated by oral LGG, providing intervention evidence that barrier permeability and
      junction-associated biology can move together under pathological conditions.
    synthesis_limitations: >-
      The review establishes mechanism rather than dietary responsiveness. The LGG experiment was performed in
      young mice with experimental Pseudomonas pneumonia, not in healthy humans, and does not establish a
      generic fermented-food effect.
    evidence_considered:
      - label: Chanez-Paredes and Turner (2023)
        citation_key: chanez_paredes_paracellular_2023
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#chanez_paredes_paracellular_2023
        data_level: Mechanistic
        evidence_source: bounded-external-search
        directional_finding: >-
          Tight junctions define size- and charge-selective pore and leak pathways; epithelial damage produces
          a separate unrestricted pathway.
      - label: Khailova et al. (2017)
        citation_key: khailova_lactobacillus_2017
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#khailova_lactobacillus_2017
        data_level: Animal Data
        evidence_source: repository-inherited
        directional_finding: >-
          Oral LGG attenuated pneumonia-induced intestinal permeability and claudin-2 elevation and supported
          mucin expression in mice.
  - id: PM1-F2
    finding_label: Butyrate can support epithelial tight-junction assembly
    presentation: mechanistic-basis
    fm_rollup: false
    finding_summary: Microbial fermentation products, especially butyrate, can act directly on epithelial barrier biology.
    finding_interpretation: >-
      This supports a Direct butyrate relationship and a Derived fermentable-fibre provision relationship,
      with microbiota and fibre-specific limitations.
    finding_statement: >-
      Butyrate can function as an epithelial metabolic substrate and promote intestinal tight-junction
      assembly, while fermentable dietary fibre lies upstream as microbial substrate provision for
      short-chain-fatty-acid production.
    synthesised_evidence_confidence: not-yet-scored
    synthesis: >-
      In Caco-2 monolayers, physiological butyrate increased transepithelial resistance, reduced inulin
      permeability and accelerated tight-junction assembly alongside AMPK activation. A broader review links
      microbial fermentation of dietary substrates to short-chain-fatty-acid production and intestinal barrier
      effects.
    synthesis_limitations: >-
      The direct assembly experiment is an immortalised epithelial-cell model. Fibre-to-butyrate conversion
      varies by fibre structure and microbial ecology, and neither source establishes a universal human intake
      threshold, a generic effect of all fibre, or oral butyrate as necessary treatment.
    evidence_considered:
      - label: Peng et al. (2009)
        citation_key: peng_butyrate_2009
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#peng_butyrate_2009
        data_level: Mechanistic

        directional_finding: >-

          assembly in Caco-2 monolayers.

  - id: PM1-F3
    finding_label: Barrier markers and attention-related symptoms are associated, not causal
    presentation: phenome-relationship
    primary_phenome: Focus / Attention Stability
    finding_summary: >-
      One small cross-sectional ADHD study linked serum zonulin with hyperactivity, but it did not establish a
      causal tight-junction-to-attention pathway.
    finding_interpretation: >-
      The evidence is compatible with the proposed relationship but is too indirect to show that changing PM1
      changes attention stability.
    finding_statement: >-
      Current human evidence provides only indirect observational support for a relationship between
      intestinal barrier biology and attention-related symptoms.
    synthesised_evidence_confidence: not-yet-scored
    synthesis: >-
      In children with ADHD, serum zonulin was independently associated with hyperactivity and social-function
      scores. A separate microbiota study found lower Faecalibacterium abundance associated with parent-rated
      ADHD symptoms, but it did not measure barrier function. Together these studies support hypothesis
      generation, not a PM1-specific causal relationship.
    synthesis_limitations: >-
      Both studies are small and cross-sectional. Serum zonulin is an indirect permeability marker; neither
      study manipulated or directly quantified tight-junction integrity, and neither demonstrates that PM1
      changes attention outcomes.
    evidence_considered:
      - label: Özyurt et al. (2018)
        citation_key: ozyurt_increased_2018
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#ozyurt_increased_2018
        data_level: Human Study
        evidence_source: bounded-external-search
        directional_finding: >-
          Higher serum zonulin was independently associated with greater hyperactivity and social impairment
          in children with ADHD.
      - label: Jiang et al. (2018)
        citation_key: jiang_gut_2018
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#jiang_gut_2018
        data_level: Human Study
        evidence_source: repository-inherited
        directional_finding: >-
          Lower Faecalibacterium abundance was associated with parent-rated ADHD symptoms, but permeability
          and tight-junction function were not measured.
    evidence_dependency:
      - >-
        The two studies address different proxies and cannot be treated as independent replications of a PM1 →
        attention relationship.
    fm_rollup: false
  - id: PM1-F4
    finding_label: Direct evidence for an Emotional Regulation relationship is absent
    presentation: phenome-relationship
    primary_phenome: Emotional Regulation

    finding_interpretation: >-
      Emotional Regulation remains a framework-level hypothesis rather than an evidence-established PM1
      relationship.
    finding_statement: >-
      The bounded evidence assessment does not establish that gut tight-junction integrity modulates Emotional
      Regulation.
    synthesised_evidence_confidence: not-yet-scored
    synthesis: >-
      Jiang et al. measured faecal microbiota composition and parent-rated ADHD symptoms. It did not measure
      intestinal permeability, tight-junction function or emotional-regulation outcomes, so it cannot directly
      support the current PM1 → Emotional Regulation proposition.
    synthesis_limitations: >-
      This is an evidence-gap adjudication, not evidence that no biological relationship exists. Targeted
      barrier measures and emotional-regulation outcomes would be needed to test the proposition.

      exposure can influence epithelial junction assembly. These separate observations motivate testing the
      joined dietary pathway; they do not establish it. The proposed five-link chain is: (1) dietary
      resistant-starch substrate reaches a capable microbial community; (2) utilisation and cross-feeding
      generate a context-dependent butyrate pool; (3) luminal butyrate becomes available to and is taken up by
      the epithelium; (4) cellular butyrate exposure engages pathways such as AMPK-related tight-junction
      assembly; (5) local engagement would produce a demonstrable paracellular tight-junction functional
      effect in the relevant host context. Evidence for separate links does not establish the complete chain.
      Moreau’s increased uptake followed healing; Peng’s cellular mechanism and the bounded human

## BRS5-1-1 - Gut Barrier / Tight Junction Integrity


## 1. Mission & Overview

### Mission

Maintain epithelial tight junction integrity and selective permeability at the gut lining.

**Intervention Dominance:** Diet-Supported. Dietary inputs are the principal group displayed here, within the study-specific boundaries. Comparative dominance is not established.

### Overview

The gut lining is a selective gate. Tight junctions, the seals between its cells, control which materials pass between them. Maintaining that selectivity helps protect the body while allowing normal exchange. Butyrate, cellular zinc and retinoid signalling affect epithelial functions in experimental models; glutamine has a condition-specific human permeability result. These findings identify different biological routes rather than a universal gut-repair supplement. [[8]](#pm-ref-8)

- **Benefits:** Selective permeability helps limit inappropriate passage across the gut lining; symptom benefits from supplementation are specific to the populations studied.
- **Implementation Notes:** Fermentable substrates can supply microbial butyrate. Nutrient adequacy differs from extra-intake benefit; the glutamine trial concerned postinfectious diarrhoea-predominant IBS with confirmed hyperpermeability.
- **Biological Relevance:** This PM concerns epithelial junction regulation. Mucus-specific microbial effects belong to PM3 and bioactive endotoxin containment to PM2. Lower electrical resistance may reflect selective ion permeability rather than unrestricted leakage.

## 2. Primary Biological Effects

↑ tight-junction strength; ↓ permeability

## 4. Mechanistic Basis

### Summary

Cellular zinc supports junction-protein maintenance; retinoic acid influences epithelial differentiation and selective permeability. [[8]](#pm-ref-8)

#### Biological process

The zinc result supports a bounded cellular requirement. Retinoid biology cannot be simplified to lower permeability in every context. [[8]](#pm-ref-8)

#### Mechanism Boundary

This PM concerns epithelial junction regulation. Mucus-specific microbial effects belong to PM3 and bioactive endotoxin containment to PM2. Lower electrical resistance may reflect selective ion permeability rather than unrestricted leakage.

#### Integration

This PM contributes its specific process to its parent FM. Shared inputs do not merge distinct jobs or prove an integrated clinical outcome.
